Dozens of AI safety incidents have come to light in recent months, with thousands more under investigation.

We can’t count on the Trump Administration to act, so I’m working with @RepZoeLofgren and @RepRaskin to ask AI companies to report incidents to Congress.

Congress needs to put real guardrails on AI, and this information will help us get it right.

“In the absence of any mandatory reporting requirements or common guidelines regarding what incidents should be reported, to whom, in what detail, and at what intervals, companies such as yours have been left to develop your own de facto standards on a voluntary basis,” [...] “And the Trump Administration has been content to rely on voluntary disclosures and self-regulation by the AI industry.”

“But that approach will not suffice; it relies too heavily on the consistent goodwill of all AI companies to voluntarily disclose incidents that might expose them to liability and reputational damage. While there is no question now that Congress must act to address gaps in AI governance, we must have the best information available to undertake that complicated process in a thoughtful and productive way.”
